title: CLID-MU: Cross-Layer Information Divergence Based Meta Update Strategy for Learning with Noisy Labels

problem.claim: Meta-learning for noisy-label scenarios needs to train robust models despite imperfect data.

gap.claim: Existing meta-learning approaches depend heavily on a clean, unbiased labeled meta-dataset that is difficult to obtain in practice.

contributions.claim: The work introduces CLID-MU, a cross-layer information divergence-based meta update strategy for learning with noisy labels without relying on a clean labeled dataset.
CLID-MU uses alignment of data structures across the last hidden and final layers to evaluate model performance and guide training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmark datasets with varying amounts of labels, under synthetic and real-world noise, report that CLID-MU outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that code is released in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Learning with noisy labels is important for training deep neural networks on imperfect data.
Existing meta-learning methods rely on a clean labeled meta-dataset, which is difficult to obtain.
The work addresses noisy-label meta-learning without a clean labeled dataset by using the data itself and cross-layer consistency signals.
Experiments under synthetic and real-world noise on benchmark datasets report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report releasing the code.

source_observation.claim: The method evaluates model performance using alignment of data structures across different feature spaces rather than requiring clean labels.

interpretation.claim: When trusted labels are unavailable, internal consistency signals may provide a proxy for identifying or managing noisy training data.

application.claim: Consider cross-representation consistency as a signal for training guidance in settings where obtaining a clean validation or meta-dataset is impractical.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when cross-layer alignment is reliable outside the reported benchmark settings or noise conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not describe the exact divergence measure, optimization procedure, or computational cost.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or generalization beyond the reported experiments.
